# Design System: DSH Agent Development Environment

## Overview

**Creative North Star: "The Dark Cockpit"**

The ADE is an operations surface: people supervise several agents at once, glance away, and come back to "what
needs me". Like an aircraft cockpit, a healthy system is calm. Calm is not grey: colour has four jobs here.
It marks what needs you, confirms a result, tells one project, provider or agent from another, and encodes data.
A colour that does none of these is removed. Everything else is ink on warm paper, dense and legible, so an indigo
diamond or a red cross is still impossible to miss.

The product is 105 plugins (the default `profiles/web` composition) mounted into one DSH Host. Its look is borrowed from the Host theme (`--dsw-*` tokens,
light and dark) and expressed through one kit, `@dshfiles/plugin-ui` (shadcn/ui on Tailwind v4 with the `dshx:`
prefix). Plugins never bring their own chrome, palette or header style; they fill one page template. Density is
"BB density": 13px body text, 28–32px controls, 6px radius; touch devices switch to a comfortable density.

Since the visual refresh (P0) `@dshfiles/ui-styles` retunes the Host theme itself: a generated
block re-tints the Host neutrals to warm stone, pins the Host aliases to one 11-step palette, remaps the Host radii and
sets Geist as the default family, so native core surfaces and plugins draw from the same values. **Light is the default
scheme; dark is equally finished.**

The plan behind this file is [docs/ade-ux/README.md](docs/ade-ux/README.md); its §3 glossary governs copy and
§4.7 the status vocabulary below.

**Key characteristics:**

- One page anatomy for every plugin page; one list row; one empty state; one field look; one tab rule.
- Colour has four jobs: attention, result, identity, data. It is never decoration and never the only carrier of a fact.
- Container-sized, not viewport-sized: every surface works from a 360px phone pane to a wide split.
- Sentence case everywhere; plugin names never appear in labels.

## Colors

The palette is **generated, not hand-picked**: `palette({ hue, chroma, accentHue, contrast, scheme })` in
`plugins/@dshfiles/plugin-ui/src/theme/palette.ts` returns 11 neutral steps in `oklch(L C 65)` (warm stone), an indigo
accent and three status trios. `scripts/emit-theme-css.ts` writes the result to
`plugins/@dshfiles/ui-styles/src/theme.generated.css`; never edit that file or restate its values. Dark chroma is
0.007 on fills and borders and 0.005 on text; light is half as warm. The dark theme is selected by
`body[data-ds-dark-theme]` and every token switches with it.

Users pick a preset in Settings › General › Appearance (Warm stone default, Neutral, High contrast, Slate blue, Moss;
`plugin-ui/src/theme/appearance.ts`), optionally override the grey hue and tint, accent hue and contrast, and choose
Geist or the system font for interface and code. The static block stays the first paint and the whole default theme;
a different choice is the same generator run in the client, injected over it. Write CSS against the tokens and it
follows every preset; never assume warm stone or indigo in a rule. Every preset keeps AA text in both schemes.

Each step has one job. Plugins reach them through the semantic Tailwind tokens; `--dshx-tone-<step>` (and
`--dshx-tone-<name>`) exist for the rare raw CSS rule.

**Surface steps.** The surfaces stay warm and step clearly apart, mostly in dark (round five): dark bg, panel, raised
and selected sit at oklch L 0.185, 0.21, 0.245 and 0.27, with the ink softened to 0.93; light panel and raised sit at
0.962 and 0.935 under the 0.992 page. Faint text (light L 0.52, dark 0.66) reads at AA on bg, panel, raised and every
row wash in both schemes.
No slate shell: navigation surfaces keep the warm stone.

| --------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | --------- |

**Prompt fill.** Your own prompt sits on `--dshx-prompt-fill`, a faint cool tint (light `oklch(0.965 0.012 230)`, dark
`oklch(0.255 0.018 230)`), 40° from the attention indigo so it never reads as Needs you; ink, secondary and faint text
and links hold AA on it (`plugin-ui/tests/prompt-fill.test.ts`). Chat's bubble reads it as `var(--dshx-prompt-fill)`.

| Signal                                             | Tailwind token | Host variable                                            | Light     | Dark      |

| Warning (hue 80)                                   | `warning`      | `--dsw-alias-state-warn-primary`                         | `#805400` | `#dca331` |

Every status is a **trio**: the colour itself for text and icons, `-bg` (12% alpha) for a tinted fill and `-border`
(30% alpha) for its border (`--dshx-tone-danger-bg`, …); badges, diff lines and error blocks use the trio, never a
solid fill. Text steps, the accent and every status colour hold WCAG AA (4.5:1) on bg, panel and raised in both
schemes; `plugin-ui/tests/palette.test.ts` enforces it. Hover and pressed washes are the ink at 6–14% alpha so they
work on any surface.

### Colour roles

1. **Four jobs.** Attention, result, identity, data. If a colour does none of them, use ink.
2. **Attention is exclusive.** The indigo diamond is Needs you and the red cross is Failed. Nothing else in a list,
   tab strip or header uses indigo or red at glyph size. Amber marks a limit or configuration that blocks a feature
   (rate limited, sign-in required, quota at 15% or less); it is never a work status.
   A page's own vocabulary is not a work status and takes no status hue: Backlog's In progress, Done and Dropped,
   a toolkit's source, a project marked Active are ink and muted shapes. Dropped is a struck ring, never the red
   cross. **Backlog status glyphs** (council round 10) are ink rings, replacing round 8's rounded squares: an open ring
   (to do), a ring holding a half-disc (in progress), a ring holding a check (done). Its status trigger is one
   status-glyph button in a 32px seat with a 10px chevron, never a checkbox look.
3. **Results are green, once.** Ready (finished, not yet seen) is a green dot with a bold title. A green check
   confirms an outcome the system verified: landed, every test passed, signed in, connection test passed. Done is a
   muted check. Working is motion, not hue: an ink ring spinner and the shimmer. Green is the glyph only; the text
   beside it stays ink.
4. **Health is one dot.** A resource that is up or down (account, host, MCP server, receiver) shows one `HealthDot`:
   green connected, amber limited, red down, faint ring off. The label is muted when healthy and takes the colour
   when not.
5. **Identity tells things apart and never says state.** Projects use the colour their owner chose
   (`--dshx-project-*`), providers and model families their brand mark, agents their avatar or a hashed
   `identity-1..8` tone. Identity colour always sits beside the name, and a list colours one identity dimension:
   the one that differs between its rows. Identity never uses `info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` or
   `chart-1..5`. A project shows as one `ProjectMark` (`components/ui/project-mark`): a 20px tile (16px dense), 4px
   radius, its tone at 18% behind two letters in that tone, with the project name beside it in muted text. The six
   project tones (hues 225, 110, 55, 305, 340, 195) keep 25° or more from every status hue.
6. **Indigo is attention, focus and links; every on state is ink.** Indigo marks Needs you, the focus ring, links and
   text selection, nothing else. The on state of a switch, checkbox or radio is `control-on`, the ink (light
   `#1b1a19`) with its tick or knob in `control-on-foreground` (white in light, `#15120f` in dark). **Dark on state.**
   In dark the on state is the ink's own hue and chroma stepped down to L 0.82 (`#c6c3c1`, `--dshx-control-on`), not
   the near-white ink (L 0.93), so a column of on switches reads as ink without glaring; the core Plugins switch follows
   the same variable. A chosen card's edge and check, and the active tab bar (2px, page tabs and the window tab strip
   alike) are ink too. Fill on bg, panel, raised and the selection wash and tick on fill hold 3:1
   (`plugin-ui/tests/control-on.test.tsx`).
   Never a button fill, never decoration. The primary button is ink.
   **Off switch.** An enabled off switch draws its boundary in the field border (`--dshx-field-border`, 1px, 3:1 on
   every surface), so an off toggle reads as a control beside the fields around it: the kit `Switch` in its own
   transparent border box, the core switch as an inset ring that never moves its knob (`ui-styles/src/client.css`). A
   disabled switch keeps the washed look with no edge.
7. **Strength ladder: mark, text, tint, fill.** A mark is a glyph, dot or logo up to 16px (20px in a header). Text
   in a colour must hold AA. A tint is the colour at 12–16% alpha behind text in that colour. Fill is reserved for
   the destructive button, the on state of a control, a provider tile up to 44px, and chart marks. A row carries at
   most one status colour and one identity colour.
   **Tint rung.** Colour sits at the tint rung on things you act on or must tell apart, never on page backgrounds,
   headers or body text. A row-level verb that answers what waits on you (Review, Answer, Rate…) is `Button`
   `variant="attention"`: Needs-you text on a 12% tint of it, no border; a failed row's verb is `variant="danger-tint"`.
   Their text is the status colour pulled 30% toward the ink so it holds AA on its own tint. A chip or band reuses
   the pair (`bg-attention-tint text-attention-foreground`). **Text rung.** A row carries one layer of colour: on a row
   that already holds its attention wash (a Needs-you or Failed thread row), the verb is `variant="attention-text"`
   (`variant="danger-text"` on a failed row): the same foreground on a transparent fill, the 12% tint only on hover
   and 18% pressed, at the size and hit area of `attention`; AA at rest, hover and press over the wash and every
   surface. Inbox CTAs (card heads, the phone's full-width verbs) keep the filled tint. **Verbs on a head band**
   (council round 12 A2): on a card's coloured head band a 12% tint disappears into the band, so a verb there takes
   `Button band`: 20% at rest, 26% on hover, 32% pressed, attention and danger alike, with its text pulled further
   toward the ink (`text-attention-band-foreground` / `text-danger-band-foreground`: the status colour 60% in light,
   50% in dark) so it holds AA on every state over the band. Both Inbox Review verbs are the same 28px trigger with the
   same padding. A selection (the selected row, the settings category, a pressed
   toggle, the palette's highlighted row, a chosen card) is `bg-selected-wash`, a neutral warm grey step with no accent
   hue, with ink text. Indigo fills mean attention only, and a selection's cue is ink too. A
   selected list row, nav item, palette row or account row adds `selected-marker` (council round 10 A2: a straight
   3 x 16px ink pill, `--dsw-alias-label-primary`, radius full, 3px from the start edge and centred on the row, painted
   as background layers so it never bends with a rounded corner; 3:1 on the wash) and sets its title at `font-selected` (550).
   **No bar beside a place tile.** Where a place glyph's tile already shows the selection (a side column row, a
   Settings category with its `PlaceGlyph`), the row draws no marker: `selected-marker` skips a row that holds a
   selected `place-seat`. **No bar beside a glyph, tile or mark.** Since council round 11 A1 a row whose first visual
   is a glyph, tile or mark draws none either (a status glyph, a project tile, a provider or model mark: the pill sat
   3–5px from it and crowded the leading column); the wash and the 550 title carry the selection, as in Linear and
   Things. **Selected edge.** Such a row adds `selected-edge` beside its wash (council round 12 A1; `SELECTED_EDGE` in
   `components/selection`): a neutral 1px inset edge, `--dshx-selected-edge` (light `#88827d`, dark `#7f7974`; the
   council's `#a39b93` held only 2.26:1 on the light wash), 3:1 against the wash on the page, the nav column and a
   dialog, because the wash alone sits about 1.1:1 off the dark page. An inset shadow, so it moves nothing. The current
   thread row and an account row take it; a pill row never does. The kit finds its own leading
   `StatusGlyph`, `ProjectMark`, `PlaceGlyph`, `ModelMark` and `NativeProviderMark`; a plugin row marks its own glyph
   with `LEADING_GLYPH_ATTRIBUTE` or opts the row out with `MARKER_OPT_OUT` (`components/selection`). Only plain-text
   rows keep the pill, and one exception: a selected Needs-you or Failed row keeps it (`MARKER_KEEP`,
   `data-marker="pill"`), because it shows its attention wash instead of the selected wash and the pill is then its
   only selection cue besides the 550 title. A chosen card or tile (a theme card, a starter) takes `selected-card`
   instead, nothing heavier: a 1.5px edge in the ink at 80% (its 1px border plus a 0.5px inset ring, so the box never
   moves; 3:1 on every card surface) and an ink check badge in its trailing top corner (16px) in the full ink, no
   wash, so the card keeps its own surface and its artwork; no leading marker. The current
   place shows strongly once: a leaf row takes the wash, marker and 550; its parent rail item only an ink label and its
   glyph in colour. Hover stays the ink wash.
   **Attention outranks selection.** A Needs-you row holds `bg-wash-needs-you` and a Failed row `bg-wash-failed` for as
   long as it is in that state: opaque washes of their hue, stronger than the selection wash, with ink, secondary and
   faint text and the status glyphs at AA on them. A full-width head band (an Inbox card's) takes
   `bg-wash-needs-you-band`, calmer in dark (chroma 0.035 where a row keeps 0.045); dark Failed is
   `oklch(0.255 0.032 25)`. A count that names a status is a `StatusCount` (the status glyph at
   10px beside a tabular number, on the tint pair for Needs you and Failed), so it reads without its colour.
8. **Data.** Categorical series use `data-1..6` in order: six identity hues at a chart step (teal, violet, copper,
   magenta, olive, cyan). The data ramp never starts with the accent, and ChartFrame maps the chart library's
   palette onto it. A status hue appears in a chart only when the series is
   that status (failed requests are `destructive`). Quota is ink while healthy, amber at 15% or less, red when
   spent.
   **Chart labels.** Axis ticks and titles, legend labels (steps and gradient ends too) and facet labels inside a
   `ChartFrame` read at the full secondary ink (`#646362`, `#a7a4a1`: AA on bg, panel and raised), 12px, tabular
   figures; the chart library's own 68–78% opacity and 10–11px are overridden, and the frame's own text is the 12px meta
   step, so no chart text is under 12px (council round 10 A8). The interactive legend takes the size only, so a hidden
   series keeps its dimmed label. Gridlines and value labels on marks stay quiet.
   **Spend map breakdown.** `SpendMap` `picker="segments"` shows one dimension at a time: a "Breakdown by" segmented
   control (Models / Accounts / Projects / Purpose) above the flow of the selected dimension only, which spans the card
   width so its labels show in full; the caption names the active metric and its unit (council round 10 D1).
9. **Diff and syntax.** The transcript's code blocks and the diff view share one syntax pair: Shiki's `css-variables`
   theme reading the `--shiki-token-*` values the theme block generates (keyword violet, function blue, string teal,
   constant copper, parameter magenta, every hue 25° or more from the status hues), each fitted per scheme to hold
   4.6:1 on the page, the code block, raised and every diff band. The diff body sits on the ramp (the page in light,
   the panel step in dark, never a near-black); in light, added and removed lines are a 16% tint of success and danger
   over it and a changed word 34% (council round 11 A3: at 12% / 20% a changed word lifted only 1.08:1 off its line;
   now 1.3:1), written as `color-mix()` over the theme tones so every preset follows and painted as is (the library's
   own line mix is off). Inside the light diff, punctuation and comments are capped at L 0.43 and the `+`/`−` marks and
   line numbers are the tone pulled 25% toward the ink, so every text, syntax colour and the ink hold 4.5:1 on lines
   and changed words alike; in dark, where
   that tint barely moved off the panel, each band is its own step in the tone's hue: calm lines at L 0.25, chroma
   0.04, and a changed word clearly lifted off its line at L 0.34, chroma 0.075 (council round 10 A4; every syntax
   colour 5.6:1 or more on both, ink 9:1). The gutter shows `+` and `−`, so a change reads without its colour. The
   collapsed-lines bar is a 3% ink wash that reaches both card edges: where it expands, a 14px chevron in the
   line-number gutter and "Show N unchanged lines" where the code starts; where it cannot (a patch without the file),
   "N unchanged lines" at the same inset and no chevron. Comments are the faint step, darkened only as far as the
   deletion band needs.
10. **Colour through meaning.** Colour enters a grey page through what it means, not as decoration: a provider's
    brand mark wherever a model or provider is named, a `ProjectMark` wherever a project is named, each theme's real
    swatch in the appearance cards, identity tones on the core Plugins icon tiles, a `StatusCount` on the Inbox title.
    No tinted page headers, panels, primary buttons or coloured section backgrounds.
11. **Navigation identity.** Each rail destination draws its glyph in its own identity tone, glyph only, and the
    active one adds a 14% tile of that tone behind the glyph with its ink label at 600; the label never takes the
    tone. `nav-tone-<id>` on the item, `text-nav-tone` on its icon and `bg-nav-tile` on the active seat
    (`plugin-ui/src/color-roles.css`). The rail has its own six tones, not the identity ramp: Work orange 52, Observe lime 118, Land teal 180, Threads blue 235, Knowledge violet 305, Agents rose 350.
    Inbox is the attention destination: its glyph is the secondary ink, like Settings, and its indigo
    `AttentionBadge` carries the colour. **Nav tone constraints** (`tests/nav-tone.test.ts`): one hue per destination
    in both schemes; light L 0.52–0.56 at chroma 0.14, dark L 0.78 at 0.13; a chroma floor of 0.12, or the sRGB edge
    where a hue ends lower (teal and blue in light, about 0.10 and 0.12), so no tone reads muddy; every hue 25° or more
    from the status hues (25, 80, 150, 270) and 40° or more from every other; every pair ΔE 0.06 or more; the glyph
    3:1 on bg, panel, raised and its own 14% tile, the ink label AA on that tile. The phone tab bar uses the same tones,
    on its current tab only.
    **Rail surface.** The rail is one surface in every state: the nav tone (`--dsw-specific-sidebar-fill`) beside a
    page on bg, whichever destination is open, whether its side column is open or folded. A destination never repaints
    the rail. **Active destination tab.** The active main tab of a destination page (Inbox, Backlog, Usage, Review,
    Settings, Plugins…) draws the destination's glyph in its nav tone on that tone's 14% tile (the selected-place
    tile below); the label stays ink and the tab takes no tint or bar colour. A thread tab keeps its `ProjectMark`.
    **Selected-place tile: a selected place carries its tone.** The rail's pattern holds wherever a place is
    selected: the selected row of the Settings column (its group's identity tone), the selected row of the Work,
    Observe and Land side columns (its destination's tone), and the active main tab put their 16–18px glyph on a 14%
    tile of that tone, a 24px seat (`PlaceGlyph`, `components/ui/place-glyph`: `tone` for a nav place, `toneColor`
    for any identity tone; or `dshx:place-seat` with your own size and radius). The seat lights from the row's own
    `aria-current`, a tab's `aria-selected="true"` or Dockview's `.dv-active-tab`, and keeps its size either way, so
    selecting never moves a row. **Phone tab bar: colour on the current tab only** (council round 12, reversing round
    9 B3: on iOS a tinted glyph means selected, so tinted neighbours pulled the eye away from the current tab). Unselected
    glyphs are the tertiary ink; the current one is drawn in its tone on its tile with a 600 label; Inbox keeps its
    badge. The desktop rail keeps its always-toned glyphs: it is a launcher, not a tab bar. The selection bar, the
    wash and the label stay neutral ink: only the glyph and its tile carry colour. Page `h1` marks stay glyph-only.
    Glyph 3:1 and the ink label AA on the tile over bg, panel, raised and the selection wash, for every nav and
    identity tone (`plugin-ui/tests/place-glyph.test.tsx`).
    **Settings group tones.** Every Settings group has its own tone, on its desktop navigation glyphs (16px) and its
    phone root tiles (28px) alike, so no group is grey: General sky 235, Models & accounts violet 300, Agents rose 350,
    Tools copper 50, Projects olive 100, Plugins teal 195, Hosts azure 215, Security orchid 325, Notifications moss 122,
    Pages aqua 170, About copper, Developer violet. Only ten hues clear the status bands, so two repeat, at least six
    groups apart. Pages and Developer rows keep each page's own icon, drawn in the group tone by `SettingsToneMark`.

Use semantic tokens only, never raw hex in plugin code. The exceptions are brand artwork
(`ai-accounts/src/account-labels.ts`, `model-effort-picker/src/brand-marks.ts`) and a project colour the user
picked. Brand marks are logos: they are exempt from contrast rules and therefore never the only label. Every
other coloured text holds 4.5:1 and every mark 3:1 on bg, panel and raised in both schemes. No pure `#000`.

A DSH bump that renames a Host variable we override fails `ui-styles/tests/host-variables.test.ts`; fix the name in
`plugin-ui/src/theme/theme-css.ts` and regenerate.

## Typography

One family, **Geist** (variable), for every surface, native and plugin alike; code and identifiers use **Geist Mono**.
Both are vendored in `plugins/@dshfiles/ui-styles/src/fonts` (latin, SIL OFL 1.1) and set through the Host's default
stacks (`--dsh-font-family-text-default`, `--dsh-font-family-code-default`), so a family typed in Settings › Font still
wins and Settings › Font size still scales everything. Read the family through `--dsw-font-family` /
`--ds-font-family-code` (`font-sans`, `font-mono`); never name a font in plugin CSS. Apply `dshx:font-mono!` on
controls because the Host's unlayered form-control rule wins otherwise. The scale is compact and steps by weight more
than size:

| Role          | Size / line                     | Weight       | Use                                             |
| ------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Display       | 26/32 (`text-display`)          | 600, -0.02em | Hero headline (new thread)                      |
| Page title    | 22/28 (`text-title`)            | 650, -0.01em | The page `h1`, exactly one per page             |
| Heading       | 15/20 (`text-heading`)          | 600          | In-page section heading: an Inbox card title    |
| Settings heading | 18/24 (`settings-heading`)   | 600          | A Settings category's sections: 40px above, 12px below |
| Section title | 13px, 15px phone (`text-sm`)    | 600          | `PageSection` `h2`, card titles                 |
| Body / UI     | 13px, 15px phone (`text-sm`) / 1.45 | 400      | Rows, descriptions, forms                       |
| Prose         | 14px, 15px phone (`text-base`)  | 400          | Assistant messages, long descriptions           |
| Label / meta  | 12px, 13px phone (`text-xs`) / 1.35 | 400–500  | Chips, timestamps, helper text, badges, keycaps, chart axes and legends |
| Dense meta    | 11px, 12px phone (`text-2xs`)   | 400–500      | Counters, graph labels                          |
| Code          | 12–12.5px mono                  | 400          | Commands, paths, ids that must be read verbatim |

The minimum is 11px; nothing smaller. Every kit text step reads a density token (`text-2xs` the minimum,
`--dshx-density-text-min`; `text-xs` `-meta`; `text-sm` `-ui`; `text-base` `-prose`), and so does `.dshx-root`, so kit
text takes the phone sizes without a phone class (see Density). Never write `text-[Npx]`; `node --run check:design-tokens` ratchets it. Descriptions cap at 72ch. Labels are sentence case; ALL-CAPS form labels are
retired. Numbers in counters, times, token counts and tables use `tabular-nums`.

### Durations

One grammar, from `@dshfiles/plugin-ui/lib/format-duration`; no plugin formats a duration itself.

| Kind                                                                              | Function               | Looks like                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Time someone waited: a turn, a tool call, a job, a subagent, an open question     | `formatElapsed(ms)`    | `9s` · `2m 05s` · `1h 04m`           |
| A measured span in a table, a trace or a test report                              | `formatDurationMs(ms)` | `420ms` · `1.5s` · `42s` · `3m 05s`  |

Whole seconds, rounded down; no space before the unit; `s`, `m` and `h` are the same in every language. Seconds are
zero-padded after minutes and minutes after hours, so a ticking clock keeps its width. A clock that ticks is a
`LiveElapsed`, which shares one timer for the page. A finished step under one second shows no duration, and a turn's
total is said once, by its "Worked for" header. `m:ss` and `2 min 5 s` are retired.

A time of day is `formatClockTime(at, { seconds? })` from `@dshfiles/plugin-ui/lib/format-clock-time`: the locale's
12/24 h choice, printed one way everywhere — `15:45` and `09:05` in a 24-hour locale (the transcript's turn time),
`3:45 PM` in a 12-hour one, never `24:00`. No plugin calls `toLocaleTimeString` with its own options, so one instant
never shows two ways on one screen.

### Density

Two densities, switched by pointer and width, never by user agent (`plugin-ui/src/styles.css`):

| Token                               | Compact (desktop) | Comfortable (coarse pointer)                  |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `--dshx-density-text-ui` / `-prose` | 13 / 14px         | 15 / 15px (phone width, a sideways phone, or `@max-pane-narrow`) |
| `--dshx-density-text-meta` / `-min` | 12 / 11px         | 13 / 12px (phone width, a sideways phone, or `@max-pane-narrow`) |
| `--dshx-density-text-input`         | 13px              | 16px (every coarse pointer: no Safari zoom)   |
| `--dshx-density-target`             | 28px              | 44px (every coarse pointer)                   |
| `--dshx-control-h`                  | 32px              | 44px (every coarse pointer)                   |

**One control height.** `--dshx-control-h` (`dshx:h-control-h`) sizes every control that sits in a row with others:
`Input`, `InputGroup`, `Combobox`, the default `Select` trigger (and `select-look`), the segmented `TabsList` root with
its items inset 3px, and default-size `Button`s, so `Page` header actions. All take one radius, 8px
(`--dsw-radius-md`, `rounded-lg`); every `Button` size shares it. `size="sm"` (28px) is for a dense row or toolbar,
never beside a field. **Toolbar fields.** In a toolbar row, a launcher or value trigger (Search threads, a filter, a
project picker) is `Button` `variant="field"` `size="field"`: the control height at 13px with a 14px glyph, so the
search field, the pickers and the filter are one 32px row on desktop and 44px on a coarse pointer. The pickers and
the filter are quiet triggers; only the search field (or a launcher that stands for it) keeps the field edge.

Safe areas: `--dshx-safe-top|right|bottom|left` (`env(safe-area-inset-*)`) on the phone top bar, tab bar, composer and
sheets. Kit buttons, toggles and menu rows already get 44px hit areas on a coarse pointer.

The phone shell (top bar and tab bar instead of the desktop rail) follows one rule,
`PHONE_SHELL_QUERY` in `plugin-ui/src/lib/phone-shell.ts`: a viewport under 640px, or a coarse pointer under 500px tall.
A phone turned sideways (844×390) keeps it. Key phone layout on that rule, not on width alone. Status lives
in a 44px top-bar status button on Threads and Inbox that opens the status sheet (with the usage ring); there is no
permanent band above the tab bar, and a strip returns only for an actionable condition (quota low, disconnected).

**Phone Settings is a drill-down.** The Settings root is a grouped list: 44px rows, each with a 28px identity tile, its
name and a trailing chevron; the first group sits 16px under the header. A category page shows only its fields, 16px
apart, under a Back control and the category name; there is no category dropdown on the page. Modified moves into
the search field's filter or the ⋯ menu, never the toolbar.

**Phone Inbox head.** Every phone Inbox card, the failed one included, takes the same two-line head. Line 1: the
status glyph, the full title (wrapping to two lines, never cut for metadata) and the ⋯ menu, whose glyph sits 22px
from the card edge. Line 2: the `ProjectMark`, the kind (Approval, Question, Turn failed…) and the age, at 13/400 in
secondary ink. Titles win over the fold. **Triage** is a worded 44px text button in the top bar's trailing seats,
beside ⋯ (council round 11 C1: its label, never an icon alone); the Needs you / Other / Done segmented row carries no
Triage control. When Needs you holds more than one status, its segment counts them as a tally (◆ 2 · ✕ 1: each
status glyph and its tabular number 4px apart, no pill, a muted dot between; `PageTab` `statusCounts`, phone shell
only), so a failure below the fold shows at first glance.

**Phone dock.** On a phone the transcript scroller ends above the dock (composer and its docked rows), never under
it: a fade one line-height tall (28px) ending exactly at the top edge of the dock's first card, so no line is half
clipped, and bottom padding that clears the last line. The jump-to-latest control is `ArrowDown` in a 28px round seat
(never arrow-to-line, which reads as download), in the dock's trailing seat or 16px above the dock's top edge outside
the text column; it is never over text. The empty composer is a 72–76px block that grows as you type.

Every control on a phone screen has a 44px hit area. Kit controls have it; a native-fork control takes the kit's
`dshx-hit-44` class. A full-screen surface on a phone has a visible way out (Cancel or ‹) in its first row. With
the keyboard up, a floating list is clamped between the top bar and the composer, and opens below the caret when
fewer than three rows fit above. Hover styles sit behind `(hover: hover)`.

## Layout

**Page anatomy** (`Page` from `@dshfiles/plugin-ui/components/page`):

```
┌ Page (its own @container; padding 24px, 12px below 28rem) ───────────────────────────┐
│ h1 Heading 22/650  12 or ◆2 ✕1  [meta chip]      [Secondary] [Secondary] [⋯] [Primary] │
│ One-line description, muted, ≤ 72ch                                                    │
│ Tab  Tab  Tab  (underline: sections · segmented: ≤ 4 view modes)                       │
│ ─ body: PageSection (h2 · meta · actions) → EntityList / form / table / EmptyState ─   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- At most one primary action. Secondary actions are outline buttons while the page is at least 42rem wide and fold
  into the `⋯` overflow menu below that; the primary never folds.
- **Two page frames, not four widths.** The header and the body share one start-aligned container: `lane`, 880px
  of content (960px once the pane is 1280px or wider, `@min-pane-wide`; the cap is the content box, the 24px padding
  sits outside it, so Inbox, Backlog and Plugins rows end on one edge), for lists (Inbox, Backlog, Plugins), never
  centred, and `wide`, min(100%, 1200px), for data (Usage, Review, AI accounts) — `Page` `width="lane"` /
  `width="wide"` (`max-w-lane`, `max-w-wide`). **Form frame.** A page of label/control rows (Settings) takes `form`:
  720px of content on the lane's inset rules (content box, padding outside, start-aligned, no wide-pane step;
  `width="form"`, `PAGE_FRAME_CLASS.form`, `max-w-form`), so a label and its value sit close and the header actions,
  the toolbar and the controls end on one edge. Selects in it share one 176px minimum width, so the control column's
  left edge is straight. All frames start at the same 24px pane inset. Only a diff, a chart or a table runs full
  bleed (`width="full"`, the default for a `fill` master–detail page); `width="page"` (1080px) is the legacy default
  that new pages do not choose. The header actions sit on the frame's trailing edge, never the window's. A page that
  owns its layout puts the standalone `PageHeader` inside the same frame (`PAGE_FRAME_CLASS.lane` / `.form` / `.wide`). The `h1` is 22px/650 (`text-title font-title`); its count is tertiary ink, or one
  `StatusCount` per status present (`statusCounts`). **Page title mark.** A destination page (Inbox, Backlog,
  Usage, Review, AI accounts, Settings…) carries one identity mark: the destination's rail glyph before the `h1`,
  18px, 8px from the title and centred on its first line, in the destination's nav tone (`Page` or `PageHeader`
  `mark` and `markTone`, a `NavToneId`; `text-nav-<id>`). A glyph only: never a tile, a tinted header or a coloured
  title, and `aria-hidden` (the `h1` names the page). Spacing scale: page padding 24px, 20px between the header and
  the body, body sections stacked 16px apart; narrow panes and phones keep 12px. Rows stay 32px, so density stays
  compact.
- Size by container, never by viewport: the page root is `@container`; children query `@max-pane-narrow` (< 28rem,
  phones and 360–480px panes) and `@max-pane-compact` (< 42rem, split layouts). Collapse order: labels become icons,
  secondary chips hide or wrap, primary text truncates, and only then does a row wrap.
- No horizontal page overflow at 390px. Filter rows scroll sideways (`overflow-x-auto`) instead of wrapping into a
  column of chips.
- Transcript measure: one 680px column. Assistant prose stops at 36em (about 72 characters at the transcript size),
  left-aligned (council round 11 C5); code blocks, cards, tool rows and the composer keep the 680px column, aligned
  left with the prose. The composer card takes the 3:1 field edge (`border-field-border`), so the main input reads as
  editable as any field. **Short code on narrow panes.** Below 448px of pane, a code block of
  12 lines or fewer soft-wraps at 12/18 mono with a continuation indent, so it reads without a sideways gesture; a
  longer block keeps horizontal scroll with the right-edge fade; the Wrap toggle flips either way. **Wrapped code.** A
  wrapped line continues 2ch right of its own statement's indent, never from column 0: the leading whitespace,
  measured per line by `CodeIndent` (`@dshfiles/plugin-ui/lib/code-indent`), reaches the wrap rule as
  `--dshx-line-indent` (the transcript's `.line` rule in `ui-styles/src/transcript.css`, the kit `CodeBlock`); without
  it the hang is the plain 2ch. A succeeded tool row shows a 16px kind glyph (`ToolCard` `kind`:
  edit, shell and subagent in identity tones; read and search neutral). A work row (a turn's "Worked for" header, a
  tool call, a summary line) is as wide as its content and no wider than that column; its duration or count follows the label after 8px, and its
  hover wash covers its own box. Only a block with a body (output, a diff, a test or job card, a question) takes the
  message column. Everything docked above the composer shares the composer card's fill, but only the editable card
  keeps the field edge: the dock's outline and its internal dividers are `border-l2` (`#dedcda` / `#2f2c29`; council
  round 12 C1, after the dividers took the 3:1 edge), on desktop and phone.
- **One Settings navigation.** While any Settings page is on stage (General or another), the side column stays open
  and lists, once each, the preference categories (General, Appearance, Keyboard shortcuts, Thread list, Layout,
  Composer, Transcript, Editor, Models & accounts…, grouped) and the Settings pages (AI accounts, MCP servers,
  Secrets, Plugins, Plugin market, Capabilities hub, Developer…). The General page has no in-page category list and
  no second "General" heading: the page header, then the selected category's fields, its sections headed with
  `text-heading`. Settings never folds the column; other one-page destinations (Inbox) may.
- **Settings rows.** Rows sit on the 720 form frame; the eye follows a label to its value through the row grammar
  (`plugin-ui/src/settings-rows.css`): `settings-row` on each row draws a 1px hairline (`border-border`) inset to the
  text edges and a full-row wash (the ghost hover fill) on hover, where a pointer hovers, and while a control inside
  has keyboard focus; the row bleeds 8px past its text so the wash has room without moving it, and the last row drops
  its hairline (`bg-none`). Type steps: `settings-heading` (section heading, 18/24 at 600, 40px above and 12px below,
  no top margin on the first; council round 10 A6), `settings-label` (row label, 14/20 at 500, ink), `settings-description` (13/18 at 400, secondary ink).
- Counts: the count beside a heading is the number of rows its list shows with no filter; a filter's count is what
  it would show; a zero is not drawn. A count the list cannot reproduce is a bug.
- One name per destination: the rail row, the tab title, the palette row and the `h1` are the same words, with no
  plugin prefix. A name means one place: Backlog's view of the items that need a decision is **Triage**, never a
  second "Inbox", and starting that pass on the phone Inbox is the same word. On a phone the top bar names the page, so the `h1` and its count hide together.

## Elevation & Depth

Flat, tonal layering. Surfaces separate by hairline borders (`border-border`) and the panel/raised steps, not by
shadow. Four elevation levels, and only the composer floats at rest:

| Level | Token              | Use                                                |
| ----- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| s0    | `shadow-s0` (none) | Everything at rest: pages, cards, rows             |
| s1    | `shadow-s1`        | The composer card, sticky bars (batch actions)     |
| s2    | `shadow-s2`        | Menus, popovers, selects, floating Dockview groups |
| s3    | `shadow-s3`        | Dialogs and phone bottom sheets                    |

**Two surface roles** (`surfaces.css`). Every navigation column — the thread list, the Settings categories, a master
list beside its detail — sits on `nav` (`--dshx-tone-nav`, also the Host sidebar fill): the panel step `#F4F2F0` in
light; in dark it is lifted to `oklch(0.225 0.006 60)` (`#1E1B19`, from the panel's `#1B1815`) so column and page
separate without relying on a hairline (**dark layering**; every text role AA, field edges 3:1 on it). A custom
theme's own panel colour stays its nav. Every page sits on
`stage`, the canvas (`#FEFCFA` / `#15120F`). Write `dshx:surface-nav` / `dshx:surface-stage` (they also set
`--dshx-surface`, the fill a fade, a badge ring or a sticky header blends into) or `dshx:bg-surface-nav` /
`dshx:bg-surface-stage`; CSS modules read `var(--dshx-surface-nav)` / `var(--dshx-surface-stage)`. The roles follow the
active theme's panel and bg steps, so a destination never picks its own grey: the same two roles in both schemes,
on every destination.

Tailwind's own step names resolve to these levels in the kit `@theme` (`shadow-xs` none, `sm` s1, `md`/`lg` s2,
`xl`/`2xl` s3), so a shadcn default draws a level, but new code writes the s-step.

Dark adds a 1px inner top highlight (`inset 0 1px 0`) to every level so raised layers read against near-black. Only
s2/s3 may add a backdrop blur. Declare depth once — a bordered card has no shadow. Stacking bands: Host modals 1000,
kit dialogs/sheets 1050, floating layers (select, popover, menu, tooltip) 1100. A kit dialog, alert dialog or sheet
dims the page with `bg-scrim`: the warm ink at 32% in light, black at 50% in dark.

Dialogs, alert dialogs and the command palette sit on `surface-dialog`: in light the page fill, the hairline and s3;
in dark a raised warm fill `oklch(0.27 0.006 60)` (`#292624`, clear of the scrim), a faint light edge
`oklch(1 0 0 / 0.08)` and one deep shadow `0 24px 64px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55)`. That fill sits on the page's selection
wash, so inside a dark dialog the selection lifts to L 0.30 and the faint step to L 0.68 (AA on that selection), and a
popover-level fill (the palette's `Command`) takes the dialog fill, so the card is one tone. **One shortcut chip.** A
keycap (`Kbd`, so `KeyHint` and the palette footer) is the same chip in both schemes and on every surface (council
round 10 A5): 20px, the raised step (`tone-2`) with a 1px `border-l2` hairline, 12/500 secondary ink with tabular
numerals, in the UI sans with the platform symbol faces before any generic fallback (`--dshx-kbd-font`), so ⌘ ⌥ ⇧
never fall to a serif face.

## Motion

One enter curve, one exit curve, five durations (`--dshx-duration-*`, `ease-enter`/`ease-exit`):

| Duration | Use             |
| -------- | --------------- |
| 80ms     | hover, press    |
| 120ms    | collapse, fade  |
| 160ms    | menus, popovers |
| 220ms    | panels          |
| 280ms    | phone sheets    |

Enter with `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`; exits take 100ms with `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)`. Under
`prefers-reduced-motion` animate opacity only. The Motion presets in `@dshfiles/plugin-ui/motion` are the code path for
anything beyond a CSS transition.

**Working** is the one looping state. Its mark is the `StatusGlyph` spinner: a faint ring with a turning arc, no colour,
one 900ms turn, every spinner on the page phase-locked to the same clock, paused off screen and still under reduced
motion. A working thread row may also sweep a 2.2s shimmer over its live activity line (`.dshx-live-shimmer`), which
pauses off screen too and is plain text under reduced motion. Any other spin or pulse carries
`motion-reduce:animate-none`.

A status glyph that changes while on screen cross-fades in 120ms; a row that just became Needs you, Failed or
Ready holds a 12% tint of that colour for 1.2s, then fades it in 280ms. Controls answer a press within 80ms.
Under reduced motion the glyph swaps with opacity only and the tint is skipped.

A state change never moves what the pointer or the eye is on. A mark that comes and goes (a tab's status glyph, the
header's live line, a status-strip count) keeps a reserved slot and cross-fades in 120ms. A notice over a list is an
overlay: opacity and 4px of travel in 120ms, out in 100ms. A dock entry reveals with `grid-template-rows` in 120ms
and never moves the input. Content inserted above the reader's position is compensated in the scroll offset. A
switch moves at once and reverts in the same 120ms if the write fails; no control is disabled while it saves. A
question card enters with opacity and 8px of travel in 220ms and takes focus at once. Under reduced motion each of
these is an opacity change only; nothing travels or resizes.

## Shapes

One radius scale for kit and native: **4 chips · 6 buttons and rows · 8 fields (input, select), cards and code · 12
composer, menus and dialogs · 16 phone sheets** (`rounded-sm|md|lg|xl|2xl`). The Host's `--dsw-radius-xs..panel` are remapped onto it
(4/6/8/12/12/16), so native bubbles, composer and panels follow. Badges and chips are full pills. Borders are 1px
hairlines; no coloured side borders.

Heights: 24 compact · 28 default control · 32 list row · 36 composer bar · 44 touch (`h-control-compact`,
`h-control`, `h-row`, `h-bar`, `h-touch`).

## Components

**Primary button — ink.** `Button` `variant="default"` is the Host brand fill (`--dshx-primary-fill`): in light a soft
warm near-black `oklch(0.30 0.01 h)` (`#312d29`, a step off the ink so it is not a black slab) that darkens to
`oklch(0.24 0.01 h)` on hover (`--dshx-primary-hover`, also the Host's primary hover), and in dark a softened warm grey
`oklch(0.88 0.006 65)` (`#dad7d3`, measured on the rendered Add account and Add plugin buttons) so the one primary is
never the brightest thing on the screen; `h` is the preset's grey hue. No kit action bypasses it with the 0.93 ink:
a Send button is the primary fill, a selected check the `control-on` ink (council round 10 A7).
Its label is the page colour at weight 500, 13:1 or more at rest and on hover. Never indigo. One per page. Header secondary actions are
`outline` `sm`; row verbs are `outline` or `ghost` `sm`, and a row verb that answers what waits on you is
`attention` (`danger-tint` on a failed row; see the tint rung); destructive verbs `destructive` and always behind a
confirmation when they lose work.

**Tabs — the rule.** Underline tabs for page sections (`Page` `tabs.variant="underline"`): secondary-ink labels on a
hairline, the active one in ink over a 2px ink bar, the same bar as the window tab strip. The segmented control only for
up to four view modes of one list. **One selected segment** (council round 10 A3): the segmented `TabsList`, the
page's sliding indicator and `SlidingSegments` share `segment-thumb`: paper (`#FEFCFA`) on the `#EBE9E7` track in light,
a raised `#302C28` on the `#23201D` track in dark, inset 3px at a 6px radius with a quiet 1px edge and no shadow, the
selected label the ink at 550 (its width reserved by `SegmentLabel`, so selecting never moves a neighbour); past four items the tabs are always underline. A filter over one list (Running /
Finished / All) is a `ToggleGroup`.

**Fields — one look.** Text-entry fields, `Input`, `Textarea` and `InputGroup` (so search), share `fieldLook`
(`@dshfiles/plugin-ui/components/ui/input`): a 1px field boundary, the page fill, the 8px radius, no shadow and no dark
fill. **Field boundary contrast.** The boundary is `border-field-border` (`--dshx-field-border`, light `#88827d`, dark
`#76706c`), 3:1 against bg, panel, raised, the nav column and the dark dialog fill (WCAG 1.4.11); checkbox and radio
edges use it too. A checkbox column in a dense table (AI accounts' "Show model") takes `Checkbox size="sm"` (council
round 11 A5): the same 16px box and 44px touch area, a 12px tick at an absolute 1.5px stroke, no shadow; in light its
checked fill is `control-on-dense`, `oklch(0.38 0.008 65)` (`#45423e`, council round 12 A3), so a column of checked
boxes stops reading as black squares (3:1 on every surface, the tick 4.5:1 on it); dark keeps the on state. Dividers and card hairlines stay `border-border`, subtle. **Quiet triggers** (council round 10 A1).
A control that opens a list and shows a value, the `Select` and `Combobox` triggers, `Button` `variant="field"` and the
`select-look` utility (a Host select the kit does not draw), shares `triggerLook`: a filled chip, `bg-trigger-fill`
(the ink at 5%, 5.2% dark, so `#f3f1ef` / `#201d1a` on the page and one visible step on a panel, the nav column, raised
or a dialog), a quiet 1px hairline at rest (`border-border`, `--dsw-alias-border-l2`; council round 11 A2: with a
transparent edge the chip vanished into its surface), the 3:1 field edge on hover and while open, and the accent edge
under the kit focus ring on focus; the box never changes. It is 32px with its chevron in secondary ink at full strength.
**A typeable combobox** beside quiet triggers (Review's "Compare against": type a revision or pick a bookmark) takes
`Input rest="trigger"` (`typeableTriggerLook`, council round 11 A4): the trigger look at rest, so the pair matches, and
the field look (page fill, 3:1 edge) on hover, while its list is open and while it has focus, so while you type.
**Field trigger.** A popover or menu trigger that shows a value rather than running an action (a date range, a purpose
filter, a project picker) is `Button` `variant="field"`: that look, its value in ink at 400 and its chevron in
secondary ink. **Filter row.** A filter row is one edged text field (the search) and calm filled triggers beside it
(council round 10 reverses round 8's all-edged row, which read as wireframe); an action beside it (Refresh) stays
`outline`. On a phone the thread list's filter row is one 44px row: the search field and one scope button (the
funnel and "Filters", or the picked project's name, with an ink count of the filters that are on) that opens one
popover holding project and status. A number with a unit is one `UnitInput` (the unit a muted inner suffix the screen
reader hears), never a number glued to a second control.

**Attention badge.** A Needs-you count on a nav glyph or a tab is one `AttentionBadge`
(`components/ui/attention-badge`, or `badge-attention` on a span): a 16px pill, tabular figures, in the attention fill
(light the Needs-you colour with white text; dark the accent hue at L 0.72 with L 0.2 text, never a white blob), with
a 2px ring in the surface it sits on (the rail's panel step; elsewhere set `--dshx-badge-ring`). It sits in a trailing
seat beside the glyph and never covers it. A zero draws nothing; past 99 it reads `99+`.

**DiffStat.** Every change count is `DiffStat` from `@dshfiles/plugin-ui/components/diff-stat`: `+N` then `−N`, sans,
tabular, 12px, additions in success and deletions in danger (AA on bg, panel, raised and the selected wash), a zero side
muted, the minus U+2212.

**EmptyState.** One sentence, centred, muted, at most one outline action. It never draws its own frame; the list or
card it sits in does. Loading is a `Spinner`, not an empty state.

**Status vocabulary** (`WorkStatus`, `StatusGlyph` from `components/work-status`). Exactly six states for every work
item — thread, subagent, job, check, workspace, host. Plugins map onto them and add detail text, never a colour of their own.

| State     | Meaning                              | Glyph                     | Row title |
| --------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | --------- |
| Working   | progressing without you              | ink turning ring (Motion) | normal    |
| Needs you | cannot continue without you          | indigo filled diamond     | normal    |
| Failed    | broke, with a recovery verb          | red cross                 | normal    |
| Ready     | finished, not yet seen or landed     | green dot                 | **bold**  |
| Idle      | seen, nothing pending                | faint ring                | normal    |
| Done      | landed or closed; workspace released | muted check               | muted     |

Every glyph sits in a 16px seat, so a row never shifts when its state changes. Needs you, Failed and Working draw at
14px; the Ready dot and the Idle ring both at 10px (the ring as wide as the dot, council round 6 A6). In light the
Ready dot is a lighter green than the ready text (`--dshx-ready-mark`, `oklch(0.55 0.13 150)`, 3:1 on every row surface)
so it is not the heaviest mark in a list; dark keeps the success tone. A count chip (`StatusCount`) draws the same glyph in a 10px seat beside its number;
a zero draws nothing.

Two glyph-only states draw but never group or sort: **stale** (dashed faint ring: a reading or workspace that may be
out of date) and **stopped** (muted square: cancelled or parked by the user).

**One status per item, on every surface.** A thread's status is computed once, by the thread list's projection; the
tab, the header, the palette and the status strip read that value and none derives its own. Status rolls up: a thread
is Working while it or one of its subagents is working, Needs you while one of them waits for an answer, and Ready
only when all of them have finished. A background job does not make a thread Working; it shows as a muted count. A
surface says a state with one of the six words or with the glyph alone: never Running, Completed, waiting or
Finished. A subagent that has finished is Done, never Idle.

**Waiting on you is Needs you, whatever asks.** A question, a tool approval and a plan review all make the thread
Needs you on every surface, the open thread included. The row's detail says which: the question's first words, or
`Approve: git push --force…`. While it waits nothing counts it as Working: not the status strip, not the browser
title, not the tool row, which reads "Waiting for approval" in place of a clock. The Inbox lists every thread the
list calls Needs you, and the two counts are equal. A failed turn stays in Needs you, in the list and in the Inbox,
until it is retried or marked Done. An approval is decided on its card, where the whole command shows; a row or an
Inbox item only opens it, and its verb is Review.

**EntityRow / EntityList** (`components/entity-row`). One row shape: `leading control · status glyph · title · muted
meta chips · trailing inline verb`, with an optional muted description line and full-width children (an output pane).
The middle is one button when the row selects; leading and trailing stay separate controls. Lists are one bordered
card with hairline dividers. In narrow panes meta wraps under the title and trailing verbs drop to their own line.
A selected row takes `bg-selected-wash` and the `selected-marker`, with its title at 550; a row that leads with its
status glyph draws no pill (council round 11 A1), only the wash, the 550 title and, as the list's current item, the
`selected-edge` (council round 12 A1); a Needs-you or Failed row holds its attention wash instead.

**Live work row** (a subagent, a background job). One row in the EntityRow shape: `status glyph · name · muted
current step · elapsed · Open`. While the work runs it lives in the dock above the composer, where it expands to its
detail and its Stop verb; the transcript keeps a record row with the same glyph and name and no clock. When the work
ends the dock row leaves and the record row takes the final state and the total (`Done · 5m 02s`). The name is the
task description its parent gave, the same string in the row, the list, the header and the tab: no generated handle,
no route or account id. One thing is never a card and a row on the same screen.
**Dock row grammar** (council round 8 C3): every dock row reads `› glyph · Label · detail · elapsed · worded link ↗`,
with one leading chevron per row: the label 13/500 sans ("Running" for a job), the detail 13 regular (a job's command
in mono). The desktop dock attaches to the composer: the composer fill (`--dsw-specific-input-major`), the dock's top
corners at `--dsw-radius-lg` and its bottom square, its outline and dividers in the quiet `border-l2` while the
editable card alone keeps the 3:1 field edge, and the card's top corners square under the dock.

**PageSection.** `h2` (section title) that names its `section` region, optional muted meta ("3 enabled") and actions.

**Focus ring.** One ring for kit and native controls: `outline: 2px solid` in the accent (`ring`), 1px offset
(-2px inside a clipping list or a tab strip), on `:focus-visible` only, no halo and no transition. It holds 3:1 on
bg, panel and raised in both schemes. `ring-ring/50` and box-shadow rings are retired; the kit sheet draws the ring
for every control. **Compound fields.** An input group or a command input is one box with one ring: the wrapper that
carries the border draws it while its field has focus (`:has(field:focus-visible)`), and the field draws none. A
command input on the top edge of a clipping palette draws its ring 2px inside, so it is never cut.

**Focus never falls to `body`.** An action that removes the focused element moves focus to its next sibling, or the
previous one at the end. A surface that closes returns focus to what opened it. A shortcut that opens a page
focuses its first field; one that opens a thread focuses its question card if one waits, else the composer.

**Keyboard.** The rail is navigation (`nav`, `aria-current="page"`): one Tab stop, arrow keys inside. Lists move
with J/K and the arrow keys. The shortcut sheet shows a chord only on the row that pressing it runs.

**Announcements.** A screen reader hears a state change once, politely: a thread becoming Working, Needs you,
Failed or Ready; "Reply ready" at the end of a turn; the result of the user's own action; the connection strip. It
never hears a clock, a streamed token, a count that follows a clock, or a tab opening. A clock is `role="timer"`
with `aria-live="off"`. A live region wraps only the words that change, never a container that holds a clock or a
toolbar. `role="alert"` is for a failure that lost the user's input.

## Connection, loading and errors

**Unknown is not empty.** Missing data never regroups, renames or recounts a row. A thread is an empty draft only
when the Host says it has no prompted turn, not when its title has not arrived. A verb that archives, deletes,
lands or cleans up is offered only on loaded, current data, and a bulk one names what it will touch and asks first.

**Connection.** One owner: settings-shell watches the socket, probes the Host and publishes `online`,
`reconnecting` or `offline` (`@dshfiles/plugin-ui/lib/host-connection`, mirrored as `html[data-host-connection]`).
One drawing: a strip with a `HealthDot`, under the top bar on a phone and at the top centre of the window on
desktop.

| State        | Strip                                                              | Dot   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----- |
| reconnecting | Reconnecting to DSH…                                               | amber |
| offline      | Not connected to DSH. What you see may be out of date. · Retry     | red   |
| back online  | Connected (2s, then it leaves)                                     | green |

While the strip shows, every `LiveElapsed` stops at its last value, spinners and the shimmer stand still, and the
verbs above are not offered. Cached threads stay readable and a draft stays in the composer. When the Host answers
again the thread list, open queries and the model catalog refetch; the page never needs a reload.

**Loading.** A Spinner or a skeleton of the final layout. Never a sentence that is true only of an empty result
("Choose a project", "Nothing needs you") before the first answer.

**A page that did not load** shows `LoadError`: one sentence that names the thing, Retry, and the cause under
Details. A destination whose plugin did not load says so in its own page, with Reload and a link to Settings ›
Plugins.

**Error copy.** One sentence from `errorSentence` (`@dshfiles/plugin-ui/lib/error-copy`):

| Cause                                            | Sentence                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| DSH cannot be reached                            | Could not reach DSH. Your message is kept; send it again once DSH is back.         |
| A request failed (HTTP 5xx)                      | Inbox did not load (HTTP 500). Retry; if it repeats, check the DSH terminal.       |
| The plugin's Host half is missing (404)          | Inbox is not available: its plugin did not start. Open Settings › Plugins.         |
| No account or key can run the model              | No AI account can run this model. Connect an account, then send again.             |
| The provider refused (4xx other than 408 or 429) | The provider's own sentence; Retry is a secondary button.                          |

Never shown: an endpoint id, `client api:`, a provider route id, an environment variable, a file path, or text
written for the model. The raw text and the code go under Details. The primary button is the one that can change
the outcome; Retry leads only when retrying can succeed.

## Language

English is the source language and the only one every plugin has; 中文 is kept where a plugin already carries it. A
sentence, a row or a chip is built from one dictionary: never join a count DSH translated to a word from a plugin.
Copy lives in the plugin's locale table, not in a component. Settings › General › Language says that other languages
translate DSH's built-in parts only.

## Do's and Don'ts

- **Do** build every page from `Page` → `PageSection` → `EntityList`/form/table → `EmptyState`.
- **Do** map plugin states onto the six `WorkStatus` values; put nuance in the detail text.
- **Do** use the glossary: thread, project, workspace, host, land, done, agent, Needs you, usage, memory
  ([plan §3](docs/ade-ux/README.md#glossary-enforced-in-copy)). `node --run check:copy` ratchets banned terms.
- **Do** write Retry (not Try again), the ellipsis character (not three dots), and an error that says what to do next
  instead of ending in the raw cause (`Could not save: {message}`).
- **Do** format every duration with `formatElapsed` or `formatDurationMs`, every time of day with `formatClockTime`,
  and take a thread's status from the thread list's projection.
- **Do** draw every disclosure with the kit chevron: `DisclosureTrigger` inside a `Collapsible`, or `dshx:disclosure`
  on a `<details>`. **Don't** show the native ▶ marker.
- **Don't** give Working a hue, colour a row for being healthy beyond its one dot, or add a second attention colour.
- **Don't** put plugin names in labels ("pulls.review: Reviews", "Thread Sidebar: Navigation").
- **Don't** use an indigo or blue primary button, an indigo selection fill, an icon tile in a page header, a
  segmented control past four items or ALL-CAPS labels. A provider's brand tile belongs to its account row and detail header only.
- **Don't** centre a page, stretch a list across a wide pane, or size a pane with viewport breakpoints (`sm:`/`md:`):
  use the page container's 1080px and 920px widths.
- **Don't** leak raw ids or absolute paths into labels; show the entity's name and keep the id in a tooltip.
- **Don't** add a control to a fixed surface. The composer bar is `+ · mode · ⋯ · model · send` with one meta line,
  the thread header is one row with one `⋯`, a reply row is copy + `⋯`. A new verb goes into the matching `⋯` menu
  or registry (composer More items, thread menu sections, reply actions), or shows only while it carries live state
  (a pending count). Every upstream batch merged on 2026-11-11 broke this rule at least once.
- **Don't** draw a second control for something that already has one (restart, find, Since you left, notifications):
  feed the existing control instead.
- **Don't** draw one thing as a card and as a row, show a generated handle or a route id as a name, or stretch a
  one-line work row across the message column.
- **Don't** insert a control or a notice in flow where it moves the row, tab or button under the pointer.
- **Do** read the connection from `useHostConnection`, show a failed load with `LoadError`, and word an error with
  `errorSentence`.
- **Do** give every control the kit focus ring, and move focus somewhere useful after an action.
- **Don't** treat missing data as empty: no regrouping, no "Nothing here", no cleanup verb while a list is loading,
  errored or offline.
- **Don't** put a clock, a toolbar or a streaming line inside a live region.
- **Don't** print an endpoint, a route id, an environment variable or model-directed text to the user.
- **Don't** give one destination two names, or draw a count its list does not show.
- **Accepted exception:** the core Plugins page is DSH's own and has no fork here; only its tab title is ours. We
  restyle it from `@dshfiles/ui-styles` through its stable hooks (`data-plugin-*` attributes, the Tag primitive's
  `data-tone`, the suffix of its CSS-module class names), never its markup: a checked Host primitives `Switch`
  (`button[role=switch][aria-checked=true]`) takes `control-on`, the ink, like every kit switch (`src/client.css`, guarded by
  `tests/core-switch.test.ts`); and `src/core-plugins.css` (guarded by `tests/core-plugins.test.ts`) gives the page the
  shared 24px inset (12px narrow) instead of a centred 960px column, draws each icon tile as an identity tone at 14%
  with the artwork in that tone (cycling `identity-1..8` by row), and makes Experimental a quiet neutral chip at 11px,
  dropped from the rows of a group whose every row is experimental (its heading says so).

Two ratchets in `check:green` and CI hold these rules: they count findings per rule and plugin and fail only when a
count rises ([repository checks](docs/repository-checks.md#design-and-copy-ratchets)). `check:design-tokens` counts
arbitrary text sizes and radii, raw colours, native icons, Tailwind's shadow step names, numeric durations, viewport
variants, solid status fills outside the kit, `chart-1..5` used as identity or decoration, numbered palette colours,
`uppercase`, spin or pulse without a reduced-motion variant, a control's `outline-none` with no focus ring, a faint
focus ring (`ring-ring/50`), and a duration formatted outside the kit.
`check:copy` counts the glossary terms, `Plugin Name:` prefixes, "Host" as the server process, package names, raw
error echoes, a transport failure or an error code echoed to the user, the non-canonical status words, "Try again"
and three-dot ellipses.
